Why Your Hibiscus Leaves are Turning Yellow (3 FIXES!) | Garden Decoded

🌿 If your hibiscus has yellow leaves with green veins still visible — especially on new growth — your soil pH is almost certainly the culprit. In this video I explain exactly what is happening inside your soil at the chemical level, how to test for it in under 5 minutes at home, and three proven methods to fix it permanently.

🌿 Even with proper watering and feeding, yellow leaves on your hibiscus plant can signal a deeper issue: soil pH. This video explains how soil pH can block nutrient absorption, causing your hibiscus plant to stay sick. We'll show you how to conduct accurate soil testing to determine your soil's pH and provide practical gardening tips on using sulfur as a soil amendment to bring your plant back to health. Give your hibiscus the care it deserves!

A hibiscus that's healthy, green, and growing — but producing absolutely no flowers — is one of the most confusing plant problems you can have. Everything looks fine on the surface. But hibiscus are very specific about what they need to flower, and even one missing condition will stop blooms entirely. results.title: Hibiscus….multiple problems but 1 solution
results.description: The hibiscus plant is beautiful and easy to grow, but it can face several problems that affect its health and flowering. Common issues include yellowing leaves due to overwatering, underwatering, or nutrient deficiency. Buds may drop before blooming because of sudden temperature changes, lack of sunlight, or irregular watering. Pests such as aphids, whiteflies, mealybugs, spider mites, and scale insects suck the plant's sap, causing curled leaves, weak growth, and poor flowering. Fungal diseases like leaf spot, powdery mildew, and root rot can also develop in humid conditions or when the soil remains waterlogged. A lack of proper fertilizer, especially potassium and phosphorus, may reduce flower production. Regular watering, adequate sunlight, good drainage, timely pruning, balanced fertilization, and pest control help keep hibiscus plants healthy and blooming throughout the growing season.

#hibiscuscare #freegardeningtips #homemadefertilizer #hibiscusblooms #budgetgardening 
 
Stop Buying Fertiliser! 5 FREE Kitchen Hacks to Get Your Hibiscus Blooming Like Crazy) | Garden Decoded

🌿 Did you know the secret to a hibiscus bursting with flowers is probably already in your kitchen bin? In this video I share 5 completely free (or nearly free) ways to feed your hibiscus and trigger more blooms — using banana peels, coffee grounds, eggshells, rice water, and compost tea. No expensive products. No guesswork. Just results.

─────────────────────────────────
TIMESTAMPS
─────────────────────────────────
00:00 — Hook & Intro
00:37 — Hack 1: Banana Peels (Potassium Boost)
01:24 — Hack 2: Coffee Grounds (Nitrogen)
02:07 — Hack 3: Crushed Eggshells (Calcium)
02:54 — Hack 4: Rice Water (Microbes + Minerals)
03:36 — Hack 5: Compost Tea (Full Spectrum Feed)
04:24 — How to Use All 5 Together
05:13 — Outro

─────────────────────────────────
WHAT YOU WILL LEARN 
─────────────────────────────────
→ Why banana peels are the #1 free potassium source for hibiscus flowers.
→ How to use coffee grounds correctly to feed without burning roots.
→ The crushed eggshell trick for stronger blooms and better nutrient uptake.
→ How rice water becomes a free probiotic feed for your soil.
→ How to make compost tea at home and why it works so well.

─────────────────────────────────
MONEY SAVED:
─────────────────────────────────
→ Average cost of branded hibiscus fertiliser: $15–$30 per bottle
→ Cost of all 5 hacks in this video: $0 — everything comes from kitchen waste
